_doc: kura#51 Phase A — every statement shape that may touch post_tag_actor_claim, and what question it answers. claim_census_gate.py matches the WHOLE normalised shape (prefix matching let a short declaration absorb a different statement and hide a path); anything unmatched REFUSES the census. Adding an entry is the census work: run `claim_census_gate.py shapes` to see what is undeclared, find the code that issues it, and name the question it answers. Questions are the plan's B'' cut — Q-A write contract / Q-B consensus+retraction / Q-C history+audit / Q-D learning input / Q-E human-override interaction. A statement that CHANGES becomes a new shape and must be re-examined; that is intended, not friction. Integer-storage native queries are outside this legacy-table census; do not reuse a legacy artifact as proof of the whole normalized access graph.

paths.shape: SELECT c.tag_id FROM post_tag_actor_claim c WHERE c.post_id = $N AND c.actor_id = $N AND c.tag_id <> ALL($N) AND NOT EXISTS ( SELECT N FROM post_tag_actor_claim o WHERE o.post_id = $N AND o.tag_id = c.tag_id AND o.actor_id <> $N)
paths.question: Q-B
paths.note: Self-scoped reap candidate: tags THIS actor still claims, no longer proposes, and no OTHER actor claims. The NOT EXISTS ranges over other actors, so it needs per-actor rows — an aggregated tag set cannot answer it. Under rev4's B''' predicate that puts anything inside the retraction window on 'raw retention'.

paths.shape: DELETE FROM post_tag_actor_claim WHERE post_id = $N AND actor_id = $N
paths.question: Q-A
paths.note: The write contract is NOT the ON CONFLICT upsert rev2/rev3 assumed: it is delete-then-reinsert of this actor's whole set, both halves in ONE transaction. The code says why append-only is wrong — a still-running actor would accumulate claims forever and permanently block another actor's legitimate reap.

paths.shape: INSERT INTO post_tag_actor_claim (post_id, tag_id, actor_id) SELECT $N, x, $N FROM unnest(($N)::int[]) AS x
paths.question: Q-A
paths.note: Bulk unnest insert with no ON CONFLICT clause; the preceding DELETE is what makes it idempotent. Any folding must preserve 'replace this actor's set atomically', not merely 'dedupe on the PK'.

paths.question: Q-A
paths.note: The continuity proof. One audited read per bucket, issued by a timer, so the census can show the instrument was alive THROUGH the window and not merely at its ends. Organic traffic cannot stand in for it: quiet hours are real (02:00 and 05:00 measured with no rows at all), so an empty bucket would be ambiguous.

paths.question: Q-E

sites.description: merge-into: carry an actor's claim to the target tag

paths.note: The FIRST update-shaped writer of this table. rev2/rev3 assumed the write contract was delete-then-reinsert of an actor's set; a tag merge rewrites tag_id in place, with NOT EXISTS standing in for the PK conflict. Any folding that aggregates actors per (post, tag) has to keep supporting that remap under the same guard. The caller sets kura.tag_actor='human' first, so this is human curation reaching into machine claims — Q-E, evidenced rather than assumed. Q-E の根拠は呼び出し側の近接ではなく、declared site が 同一トランザクション内で kura.tag_actor マーカーを立てていること (set_config(..., true) は transaction-local、間に commit が無い)。test_the_human_marker_is_set_in_the_same_transaction が固定する。
